summary: A Java JSON web service on Spring Boot and Maven with one error format, request logs and null checks at compile time.
description: Write a Java HTTP service on Spring Boot with Maven. One in-memory notes resource proves the shape: create, read and paged list routes, strict JSON input, and one error envelope for bad input, misses, wrong methods and unexpected failures, all from a single error table. Request ids, JSON access logs, validated settings and Actuator come wired. The build formats code, catches nullness bugs and common mistakes at compile time, enforces a coverage floor and checks the layering with ArchUnit. The recipe picks no database, sign-in or hosting; the store sits behind an interface a database can implement.
seoDescription: A Spring Boot API recipe in Java with Maven, one JSON error envelope, request ids and logs, NullAway and Error Prone, slice and integration tests.

projectExamples.title: Internal inventory service
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: replace notes with stock records that other services read and update over HTTP. Persistence and access control are work the project still has to add.

plain.whatItIs: A starter web service written in Java that answers requests with JSON data, with clear error replies, request logs and a health check for monitoring.
goodAt: Backends that websites, phone apps or other services call for data
Teams that already run Java services and want the same conventions
Services that must report every error in one consistent format
notGoodAt: Projects that need a database or sign-in from the start; you add both yourself.
Pages and screens for people to click through; use a web app stack for those.

The first build downloads every dependency and plugin, which takes a few minutes.
